      <content name="title">Older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adult</span></span> Mental Health</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Emotional Health</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Mental Health, Older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adults</span></span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Seniors' Mental Health</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Senior mental health</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Mental health includes our emotional, psychological, and social well-being. It affects how we think, feel, and act as we cope with life. It also helps determine how we handle stress, relate to others, and make choices. Mental health is important at every stage of life, including as we age.</p><p>Many older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> are at risk for mental health problems. But this does not mean that mental health problems are a normal part of aging. Studies show that most older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> feel satisfied with their lives, even though they may have more illnesses or physical problems.</p><p>Sometimes, however, important life changes can make you feel uneasy, stressed, and sad. These changes could include the death of a loved one, retirement, or dealing with a serious illness. Many older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> will eventually adjust to the changes. But some people will have more trouble adjusting. This can put them at risk for mental disorders such as depression and anxiety.</p><p>It's important to recognize and treat mental disorders in older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span>. These disorders don't just cause mental suffering. They can also make it harder for you to manage other health problems. This is especially true if those health problems are chronic.</p><p>Some of the warning signs of mental disorders in older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> include:</p><ul><li>Changes in mood or energy level</li><li>A change in your eating or sleeping habits</li><li>Withdrawing from the people and activities you enjoy</li><li>Feeling unusually confused, forgetful, angry, upset, worried, or scared</li><li>Feeling numb or like nothing matters</li><li>Having unexplained aches and pains</li><li>Feeling sadness or hopelessness</li><li>Smoking, drinking, or using drugs more than usual</li><li>Anger, irritability, or aggressiveness</li><li>Having thoughts and memories that you can't get out of your head</li><li>Hearing voices or believing things that are not true</li><li>Thinking of harming yourself or others</li></ul><p>If you think that you may have a mental health problem, get help. Talk therapy and/or medicines can treat mental disorders. If you don't know where to start, contact your primary care provider.</p></content>

    <document rank="1" url="https://medlineplus.gov/vaccines.html">
      <content name="title">Vaccines</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle"><span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adult</span></span> Immunization</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Immunization, <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adult</span></span></content>
      <content name="altTitle">Immunization</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Vaccination</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What are vaccines?<p>Vaccines are injections (shots), liquids, pills, or nasal sprays that you take to teach your body's immune system to recognize and defend against harmful germs. For example, there are vaccines to protect against diseases caused by:</p><ul><li>Viruses, like the ones that cause the flu and COVID-19</li><li>Bacteria, including tetanus, diphtheria, and pertussis</li></ul>What are the types of vaccines?<p>There are several types of vaccines:</p><ul><li>Live-attenuated vaccines use a weakened form of the germ.</li><li>Inactivated vaccines use a killed version of the germ.</li><li>Subunit, recombinant, polysaccharide, and conjugate vaccines use only specific pieces of the germ, such as its protein, sugar, or casing.</li><li>Toxoid vaccines use a toxin (harmful product) made by the germ.</li><li>mRNA vaccines use messenger RNA, which gives your cells instructions for how to make a protein (or piece of a protein) of the germ.</li><li>Viral vector vaccines use genetic material, which gives your cells instructions for making a protein of the germ. These vaccines also contain a different, harmless virus that helps get the genetic material into your cells.</li></ul><p>These vaccines may work in different ways, but they all spark an immune response. The immune response is the way your body defends itself against substances it sees as foreign or harmful. These substances include germs that can cause disease.</p>What happens in an immune response?<p>There are different steps in the immune response:</p><ul><li>When a germ invades, your body sees it as foreign.</li><li>Your immune system helps your body fight off the germ.</li><li>Your immune system also remembers the germ. It will attack the germ if it ever invades again. This "memory" protects you against the disease that the germ causes. This type of protection is called immunity.</li></ul>What are immunization and vaccination?<p>Immunization is the process of becoming protected against a disease. But it can also mean the same thing as vaccination, which is getting a vaccine to become protected against a disease.</p>Why are vaccines important?<p>Vaccines are important because they protect you against many diseases. These diseases can be very serious. So getting immunity from a vaccine is safer than getting immunity by being sick with the disease.</p><p>For a few vaccines, getting vaccinated can actually give you a better immune response than getting the disease would.</p><p>But vaccines don't just protect you. They also protect the people around you through community immunity.</p>What is community immunity?<p>Community immunity, or herd immunity, is the idea that vaccines can help keep communities healthy.</p><p>Normally, germs can travel quickly through a community and make a lot of people sick. If enough people get sick, it can lead to an outbreak. But when enough people are vaccinated against a certain disease, it's harder for that disease to spread to others. This type of protection means that the entire community is less likely to get the disease.</p><p>Community immunity is especially important for people who can't get certain vaccines. For example, they may not be able to get a vaccine because they have weakened immune systems. Others may be allergic to certain vaccine ingredients. And newborn babies are too young to get some vaccines. Community immunity can help to protect them all.</p>Are vaccines safe?<p>Vaccines are safe. They must go through extensive safety testing and evaluation before they are approved in the United States.</p>What is a vaccine schedule?<p>A vaccine, or immunization, schedule lists which vaccines are recommended for different groups of people. It includes who should get the vaccines, how many doses they need, and when they should get them. In the United States, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) publishes the vaccine schedule.</p><p>It's important for both children and <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> to get their vaccines according to the schedule. Following the schedule allows them to get protection from the diseases at exactly the right time.</p></content>

    <document rank="2" url="https://medlineplus.gov/exerciseforolderadults.html">
      <content name="title">Exercise for Older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adults</span></span></content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Fitness</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Seniors' Fitness</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>Exercise and physical activity are good for just about everyone, including older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span>. There are four main types and each type is different. Doing them all will give you more benefits.:</p><ul><li>Endurance, or aerobic, activities increase your breathing and heart rate. Brisk walking or jogging, dancing, swimming, and biking are examples.</li><li>Strength exercises make your muscles stronger. Lifting weights or using a resistance band can build strength.</li><li>Balance exercises help prevent falls</li><li>Flexibility exercises stretch your muscles and can help your body stay limber</li></ul><p>If you have not been active, you can start slowly and work up to your goal. How much exercise you need depends on your age and health. Check with your health care provider on what is right for you.</p><p>NIH: National Institute on Aging</p></content>

    <document rank="3" url="https://medlineplus.gov/nutritionforolderadults.html">
      <content name="title">Nutrition for Older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adults</span></span></content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Seniors' Nutrition</content>
      <content name="FullSummary">What is nutrition and why is it important for older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span>?<p>Nutrition is about eating a healthy and balanced diet so your body gets the nutrients that it needs. Nutrients are substances in foods that our bodies need so they can function and grow. They include carbohydrates, fats, proteins, vitamins, minerals, and water.</p><p>Good nutrition is important, no matter what your age. It gives you energy and can help you control your weight. It may also help prevent some diseases, such as osteoporosis, high blood pressure, heart disease, type 2 diabetes, and certain cancers.</p><p>But as you age, your body and life change, and so does what you need to stay healthy. For example, you may need fewer calories, but you still need to get enough nutrients. Some older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> need more protein.</p>What can make it harder for me to eat healthy as I age?<p>Some changes that can happen as you age can make it harder for you to eat healthy. These include changes in your:</p><ul><li>Home life, such as suddenly living alone or having trouble getting around</li><li>Health, which can make it harder for you to cook or feed yourself</li><li>Medicines, which can change how food tastes, make your mouth dry, or take away your appetite</li><li>Income, which means that you may not have as much money for food</li><li>Sense of smell and taste</li><li>Problems chewing or swallowing your food</li></ul>How can I eat healthy as I age?<p>To stay healthy as you age, you should:</p><ul><li>Eat foods that give you lots of nutrients without a lot of extra calories, such as
		<ul><li>Fruits and vegetables (choose different types with bright colors)</li><li>Whole grains, like oatmeal, whole-wheat bread, and brown rice</li><li>Fat-free or low-fat milk and cheese, or soy or rice milk that has added vitamin D and calcium</li><li>Seafood, lean meats, poultry, and eggs</li><li>Beans, nuts, and seeds</li></ul></li><li>Avoid empty calories. These are foods with lots of calories but few nutrients, such as chips, candy, baked goods, soda, and alcohol.</li><li>Pick foods that are low in cholesterol and fat. You especially want to try to avoid saturated and trans fats. Saturated fats are usually fats that come from animals. Trans fats are processed fats in stick margarine and vegetable shortening. You may find them in some store-bought baked goods and fried foods at some fast-food restaurants.</li><li>Drink enough liquids, so you don't get dehydrated. Some people lose their sense of thirst as they age. And certain medicines might make it even more important to have plenty of fluids.</li><li>Be physically active. If you have started losing your appetite, exercising may help you to feel hungrier.</li></ul>What can I do if I am having trouble eating healthy?<p>Sometimes health issues or other problems can make it hard to eat healthy. Here are some tips that might help:</p><ul><li>If you are tired of eating alone, try organizing some potluck meals or cooking with a friend. You can also look into having some meals at a nearby senior center, community center, or religious facility.</li><li>If you are having trouble chewing, see your dentist to check for problems</li><li>If you are having trouble swallowing, try drinking plenty of liquids with your meal. If that does not help, check with your health care provider. A health condition or medicine could be causing the problem.</li><li>If you're having trouble smelling and tasting your food, try adding color and texture to make your food more interesting</li><li>If you aren't eating enough, add some healthy snacks throughout the day to help you get more nutrients and calories</li><li>If an illness is making it harder for you to cook or feed yourself, check with your health care provider. He or she may recommend an occupational therapist, who can help you find ways to make it easier.</li></ul><p>NIH: National Institute on Aging</p></content>

    <document rank="4" url="https://medlineplus.gov/olderadulthealth.html">
      <content name="title">Older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">Adult</span></span> Health</content>
      <content name="organizationName">National Library of Medicine</content>
      <content name="altTitle">Aging</content>
      <content name="FullSummary"><p>People in the U.S. are living longer than ever before. Many older <span class="qt0"><span class="qt1">adults</span></span> live active and healthy lives. But there's no getting around one thing: as we age, our bodies and minds change. You need to know what to expect. Some changes may just be part of normal aging, while others may be a warning sign of a medical problem. It is important to know the difference, and to let your health care provider know if you have any concerns.</p><p>Having a healthy lifestyle can help you to deal with normal aging changes and make the most of your life. This includes healthy eating, regular physical activity, and making mental health a priority.</p></content>
